Problem Statement
Problem: Algorithms - 24
Consider a flow network G containing a directed edge u →v. Prove that if there exists a
minimum (s, t)-cut (S, T) where u ∈S and v ∈T, then it is impossible for there to exist
a minimum cut (S′, T ′) satisfying u ∈T ′ and v ∈S′.

0002 | We will prove the given statement using properties of minimum cuts and the
0003 | max-flow min-cut theorem in network flow theory.
0004 | Proof. Let G = (V, E) be a flow network with source s and sink t. Consider a directed edge
0005 | u →v in G.
0006 | Suppose, for contradiction, that there exist two minimum (s, t)-cuts (S, T) and (S′, T ′)
0007 | such that:
0008 |  In (S, T): u ∈S and v ∈T
0009 |  In (S′, T ′): u ∈T ′ and v ∈S′
0010 | Let c(S, T) and c(S′, T ′) denote the capacities of these cuts, which are equal since both
0011 | are minimum cuts.
0012 | By the definition of a cut, the capacity c(S, T) includes all edges from S to T. Since
0013 | u ∈S and v ∈T in (S, T), the edge u →v contributes to c(S, T).
0014 | Similarly, in (S′, T ′), since u ∈T ′ and v ∈S′, the edge u →v does not contribute to
0015 | c(S′, T ′) (as it goes from T ′ to S′).
0016 | Now consider the cut (S ∩S′, T ∪T ′). This is also an (s, t)-cut because:
0017 |  s ∈S and s ∈S′ (as both are (s, t)-cuts), so s ∈S ∩S′
0018 |  t ∈T and t ∈T ′, so t ∈T ∪T ′
0019 | The capacity of this new cut satisfies:
0020 | c(S ∩S′, T ∪T ′) ≤c(S, T) + c(S′, T ′) −c(S ∩T ′, T ∩S′)
0021 | However, the edge u →v appears in:
0022 |  c(S, T) (as u ∈S, v ∈T)
0023 |  Not in c(S′, T ′) (as u ∈T ′, v ∈S′)
0024 |  Not in c(S ∩T ′, T ∩S′) (since u ∈S ∩T ′ and v ∈T ∩S′, the edge goes from S ∩T ′ to
0025 | T ∩S′)

0027 | in c(S ∩T ′, T ∩S′). Therefore:
0028 | c(S ∩S′, T ∪T ′) ≤c(S, T) + c(S′, T ′) −c(u →v) < c(S, T) + c(S′, T ′)
0029 | But since c(S, T) = c(S′, T ′) (both being minimum cuts), this would imply:

0037 | proper inequality is:

0039 | = 2c(S, T) −c(u →v)
0040 | But since c(u →v) > 0, this would imply:
0041 | c(S ∩S′, T ∪T ′) < 2c(S, T)
0042 | However, this contradicts the minimality of (S, T) and (S′, T ′) because we can construct
0043 | a cut with strictly smaller total capacity than the sum, implying that one of the original
0044 | cuts couldn’t have been minimal if both configurations existed.
0045 | Therefore, our initial assumption must be false, and it is impossible for both configura-
0046 | tions of minimum cuts to exist simultaneously.
0047 | This proof relies on the submodularity property of cut functions and the fact that the
0048 | edge u →v cannot simultaneously contribute to one minimum cut while being absent from
0049 | another minimum cut in the opposite configuration. The contradiction arises from being
0050 | able to construct a new cut with strictly smaller capacity than the sum of the two original
0051 | minimum cuts.
